$comment: THE DECLARED SOURCE LIST (L-1720). This file is DATA, reviewed in a diff — never a
hard-coded array inside a script, and never an ad-hoc download. `acquire.mjs` acquires
EXACTLY what is declared here and refuses anything that is not.
LICENCE RULE (C100 §10.6 MUST, PASCAL-FINISHES-RESEARCH §0.2): every entry names a source
library whose licence is declared in `libraries` below and re-asserted at acquisition time.
NOTHING is sourced from github.com/pascalorg/editor — its 288 texture files carry zero
attribution and MIT does not cure unestablished provenance. We take the TAXONOMY only.
realWorldSizeM (C100 §10.2.c `tiling`): the physical size of ONE texture tile, in metres.
A map without this is wallpaper, not a material. Two origins, and the difference is
'source-metadata' - leave realWorldSizeM null; acquire.mjs takes ambientCG's declared
'estimate'        - the source declares 0x0. The value below is a HUMAN ESTIMATE and is
stamped as such in the manifest. It must be declared HERE, in the
diff, so an estimate can never be mistaken for a measurement.

ambientcg.name: ambientCG
ambientcg.licenceVerifiedQuote: You can copy, modify, distribute and perform the assets, even for commercial purposes, all without asking permission.

$mapComment: Canonical map names match MAT-1's declared MaterialRecord.maps shape:
color, normal, roughness, metalness, ao, displacement
`normal` is always taken from the source's *NormalGL* file - three.js uses the OpenGL
green-up convention. Taking NormalDX inverts lighting on every sloped texel.

materials.label: Mosaic · Hexagon Pool Blue 069
materials.$note: C100 §10.3.a names mosaic at 1 row with NO pool tile as a measured thinness. This is the pool tile.

materials.label: External Render · Rough Stucco 001
materials.$note: C100 §10.3.a: external render/stucco is at LITERALLY ZERO and is the commonest external finish in the Spanish/Mediterranean markets the geospatial stack targets.
materials.sizeEstimateBasis: Source declares dimensionX/Y = 0. 2 m x 2 m is a conventional facade-render sample patch; the texture is stochastic (no repeating unit), so scale is a judgement of grain size, not of a module.

materials.label: Plaster · Rough White 003
materials.sizeEstimateBasis: Source declares dimensionX/Y = 0. Stochastic internal plaster; 2 m x 2 m keeps the grain plausible at room scale.

materials.$note: C100 §10.3.a: carpet is at LITERALLY ZERO despite a Fabric & Soft category that holds only furnishing textiles.

$knownGaps: FIBRE-CEMENT CLADDING (C100 §10.3.a, at LITERALLY ZERO) is NOT in this list. Measured 2026-08-21: ambientCG returns zero results for 'fibre cement' and 'fiber cement'. Not acquirable from a CC0 library today; needs either a different CC0 source or MAT-3's procedural route. NAMED, not silently dropped.

PATTERN SUB-TYPE (herringbone vs chevron vs basketweave vs versailles) is NOT present in any source metadata field. Labels above are derived from the source's own displayName and tags, never invented. Assigning a pattern sub-type needs a HUMAN VISUAL PASS over the acquired colour maps.
